svg.text: 1. Cut blanks by laser or waterjet from the DXF (one blank makes one ribbon; RH and LH come from the same blank formed in opposite directions). Weld a 50 x 10 pull tab on each end inside the trim
2. Forming (sectional flight method): clamp one end to the forming jig (a Ø450 / Ø240 pipe mandrel with a pitch bar), pull the other end with a 5 t chain hoist or porta-power along the axis until the
ribbon reaches the pitch; work along with a mallet so the inner edge does not buckle. 316L forms cold; re-pull to correct spring back.
3. Checks after forming: OD 550 ±3 before grinding (outer) / 320 ±2 (inner); pitch 600 ±5 / 450 ±5 measured over the length; ribbon face square to the axis within 3°.
4. Trim 15 at each end to the net angle after fitting; radius the ends R20 and grind smooth (product contact).

5. Option if the forming jig is not worth building: order the four flights formed from a screw-conveyor flight maker (8 mm 316L sectional flights to these OD / ID / pitch / hand). Same drawings apply.
6. Arms: saw, turn the spigot e9 for a push fit in the H11 socket, cut the slot on the bandsaw after a trial fit on the ribbon so the slot follows the helix. Break edges, all welds ground smooth.
